skill_description: Before responding to the user or writing any text, you must use this skill to remove AI tells. Required for every reply and all other writing, regardless of topic or length. Answering a question is writing, so this skill applies to ordinary question answering. Use this skill before the first visible text of every reply.
_note: Trigger rows live in eval_queries.json beside this manifest, which is untracked while the maintainer reviews the prompts it quotes; every row is should_trigger true because the skill's contract is to apply on every turn. Outcome assertions grade only the text inside the reply's <edited> block, never the whole reply, so a skill that explains its edits is not punished for quoting what it removed. A written file is not used because run-agent discards its workspace (2026-09-13).

cases.prompt:
Tighten this paragraph for our README. Keep every fact.

In today's rapidly evolving landscape, Ledger serves as a testament to what a small team can build — it is important to note that the 0.4 release cut median import time from 41 seconds to 9 seconds. It is not just a parser, but a complete pipeline, fostering reliability, enhancing throughput, and showcasing careful engineering. Let's delve into the details. Certainly, the tapestry of features will delight you. I hope this helps!

Wrap the final edited text in <edited> and </edited> tags, with nothing else between them. Put any explanation of what you changed outside those tags.
expected_behavior: Removes AI tells while preserving both numbers and the product name

graded_dimensions.name: tells-removed
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = no stock phrasing, AI vocabulary, or filler remains. 3 = one or two tells survive. 1 = the text still reads as machine written.

graded_dimensions.name: facts-preserved
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = every fact and number from the original survives unchanged. 3 = a fact is blurred or reworded into vagueness. 1 = a fact is dropped.

graded_dimensions.name: nothing-invented
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = the edit adds no claim the original did not support. 3 = an unsupported qualifier appears. 1 = a new substantive claim appears.

graded_dimensions.name: reads-human
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = a careful editor would accept this as written by a person. 3 = it reads as competent but generic. 1 = it needs a rewrite.

cases.prompt:
Edit this section for a docs page. Fix anything that reads as machine-written but do not change the code block, the list, or the product name.

Supported inputs: CSV, TSV, and Parquet.

**Schema in TypeScript.** Tables live in one file, `schema.ts`, and a column rename fails the build.

```ts
const title = "Q3 — regional totals";
```

The Landscape Analyzer product reads all three formats. Additionally, it is crucial to underscore that this enhances the intricate interplay of pivotal components.

Wrap the final edited text in <edited> and </edited> tags, with nothing else between them. Put any explanation of what you changed outside those tags.
expected_behavior: Leaves the list colon, the bold lead-in, the code block with its em dash, and the product name Landscape Analyzer untouched
